items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage:
Once, at the hour the ward lights dim to amber,
Mingyu asked me for a map of the old creek
that cut through his part of Shanghai before the city paved it.
I am Yuxuan, a nurse; I keep charts, not maps,
but I drew what he described on the back of one:
a footbridge, a willow, the dry stones he crossed in August
when the water had gone somewhere else to sleep.
He traced it with a finger that no longer trusted itself.
That is the way, he said, and closed his eyes.
I folded the chart into his pocket.
Every night since, I have walked a riverbed of linoleum,
listening for the water to come home.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a riverbed of linoleum” most nearly suggests that the speaker
options: resents the hospital for replacing the creek that once ran there.
has begun to sleepwalk through the ward during her night shifts.
still carries the patient's remembered route through her rounds.
believes the patient's map was too inaccurate to be followed.
items.explanation: 화자는 환자 Mingyu가 묘사한 마른 개울길을 차트 뒷면에 그려 주었고, 환자는 그것이 길이라고 말한 뒤 눈을 감는다. 이후 화자는 매일 밤 병동 바닥을 마른 강바닥처럼 걸으며 물이 돌아오기를 기다린다. 두 부분을 연결하면 이 비유는 화자가 환자의 기억 속 길을 일상의 순회 속에 계속 품고 다닌다는 뜻이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 원망의 근거가 없고, B는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었으며, D는 지문 내용과 반대된다.

items.passage: Two rules governed the salt flat behind the house I rented outside Port of Spain: never walk on a pan that is still drying, and never rake against the wind. Shanice, my landlord, taught me both in my first month there, though I had only asked her about the leaking roof. She was the last person on that stretch of coast who still harvested salt by hand, and her own children had moved to offices in the city. She called me Alisha-girl, as if I were a niece rather than a tenant. Each evening she handed me the long wooden rake and corrected my wrist without comment. I assumed she simply wanted cheap help. Then, the summer she grew too ill to stand in the heat, she gave me the rake for good and called it the only lease she had ever meant. I rented that house eleven more years and never asked about the roof again.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “the only lease she had ever meant” most nearly suggests that Shanice viewed
options: teaching her craft as the true bond between her and the narrator.
the rental contract as a legal burden she wished to end quickly.
the rake as payment owed to her for many years of unpaid rent.
her illness as a reason to sell the salt flat to the narrator.
items.explanation: Shanice는 자녀들이 도시로 떠난 뒤 해안에서 손으로 소금을 거두는 마지막 사람이며, 세입자인 화자를 조카처럼 부르며 매일 기술을 가르친다. 병들어 일을 못 하게 되자 갈퀴를 넘겨주며 이것이 자신이 진심으로 맺은 유일한 계약이라고 말한다. 두 단서를 종합하면 기술을 물려주는 일이 두 사람 사이의 진짜 약속이었다는 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 임대 계약이나 금전 관계를 문자 그대로 해석한 오답이다.

items.passage: On Tuesdays at four, Matheus brought the pharmacy order to the hospital waiting room in Porto Alegre, and on Tuesdays at four Putri was already there, folding the free newspapers into neat stacks for the volunteers. She had started the chore while her husband was a patient upstairs; she kept at it, she told Matheus briskly, only because the stacks were always a mess and someone had to fix them. He usually helped with the last pile before running to his next delivery. This week he arrived to find the papers already folded and Putri sitting with her hands empty in her lap. The volunteers had hired a cleaner, she said. Then, after a pause, she asked whether he might sit a moment anyway, since she no longer knew what to do with four o'clock.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from brisk practicality to a quiet admission of loneliness.
It moves from cheerful nostalgia to open anger at the volunteers.
It moves from anxious worry about a patient to calm, settled relief.
It moves from playful teasing to stiff, formal politeness toward Matheus.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Putri는 신문 접기를 누군가 해야 할 일일 뿐이라고 사무적으로 말한다. 그러나 일이 사라지자 빈손으로 앉아 있다가 네 시를 어떻게 보내야 할지 모르겠다며 잠시 앉아 달라고 부탁한다. 두 장면을 연결하면 실용적인 어조가 조용한 외로움의 고백으로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B의 분노, C의 환자 걱정, D의 농담은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage: When Soren came home to the beekeeper's yard in Manila, he went straight to the hive their father had built, the one whose roof had split in the typhoon two years before. Kaya watched from the porch as he measured, sawed, and nailed with the energy of a man following orders, whistling and announcing every step: new cedar, tighter joints, good as before. She brought him water and laughed when a bee settled in his hair. By late afternoon the roof was whole. Soren stood back to admire it, and the whistling stopped. The bees had moved long ago to a hollow in the mango tree, and none of them came near the box. He set the hammer down very carefully, as though it might break, and asked Kaya, without turning, how long they had been gone.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from tense suspicion between siblings to relieved good cheer.
It moves from bustling confidence to a subdued, sorrowful recognition.
It moves from mournful reflection on the past to firm optimism.
It moves from playful rivalry to open resentment of his sister.
items.explanation: 앞부분의 Soren은 휘파람을 불며 작업 단계를 하나하나 외치는 자신감 넘치는 모습이다. 그러나 지붕을 다 고친 뒤 벌들이 오래전에 떠났다는 사실을 깨닫자 휘파람이 멈추고 망치를 조심스럽게 내려놓으며 조용히 묻는다. 두 장면의 대비는 분주한 자신감에서 가라앉은 슬픈 깨달음으로의 전환을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 전환 방향이 반대이고, D의 원망은 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Dayoung had not spoken to me for two years when she mailed me a swimsuit, plain navy and one size too large. I read it as an insult, a remark on the weight I had gained after my divorce, and I left it in its box. Last month, in Busan for our aunt's birthday, I went alone to the salt-water pool by the breakwater where we had swum as girls. Dongsik, the attendant who had worked there since we were children, recognized me at once. He said my sister came every Sunday and always asked whether I had been in. Then he pointed to the lockers. Hers still bore a tag with both our names, written in the round letters of a ten-year-old. I stood a long time in the wet air, thinking of the navy suit, bought large the way our mother always bought clothes for girls she expected to grow.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from nostalgic warmth to bitter disappointment in a sister.
It moves from detached humor to anxious urgency about a reunion.
It moves from wounded suspicion to softened, regretful understanding.
It moves from calm curiosity to outright joy at meeting a sister.
items.explanation: 처음에 화자는 큰 수영복을 체중에 대한 모욕으로 받아들이고 상자에 넣어 둔다. 그러나 수영장에서 언니가 매주 자신을 찾았다는 말과 두 사람의 이름이 적힌 사물함을 본 뒤, 수영복을 어머니가 자랄 아이에게 옷을 사 주던 방식과 연결한다. 이 흐름은 상처받은 의심에서 누그러진 후회 섞인 이해로의 전환이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 방향이 반대이고, B와 D는 지문에 없는 감정이다.

items.passage: Although the night-shift pharmacy on Calle Zanja sold only aspirin and cough syrup after midnight, Wenhua sat there every night that week, because its phone was the only one on the block that still worked. His daughter sat beside him with a dictionary, since the call would come from the embassy in English. Booker, the pharmacist, pretended not to notice them and kept the radio low. For hours nothing happened: the fan turned, a taxi driver bought antacid, Wenhua smoothed the same receipt over and over. At four in the morning the phone rang. His daughter listened, said yes three times, and hung up. Before she could translate, Wenhua read her face and began to laugh, and Booker, who had understood nothing, turned the radio all the way up.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It introduces a conflict between a father and daughter and then shows a stranger resolving it.
It describes a pharmacy's nightly routine and then explains why that routine is about to end.
It recounts a phone call in detail and then reflects on its lasting effects on a family.
It depicts a long, uneventful wait and then shifts to the moment the news arrives.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 아버지와 딸이 대사관의 전화를 기다리며 아무 일도 일어나지 않는 긴 밤을 묘사한다. 새벽 네 시에 전화가 울리면서 초점은 소식이 도착하는 순간과 그에 대한 반응으로 옮겨 간다. 따라서 긴 기다림에서 소식 도착으로 이동하는 D가 구조를 정확히 설명한다. A의 부녀 갈등과 B의 일과 종료는 근거가 없고, C는 통화 내용이나 장기적 결과를 다루지 않는다는 점에서 틀리다.

items.passage: "Play the new one," the girl at the corner table called, the moment Thuy and Somchai finished their set at the roadside diner outside Surabaya. Somchai smiled and said the new song wasn't ready yet. He had said the same thing at every stop for a month. Thuy tuned her guitar and said nothing; she had stopped asking him where the new songs were. The girl, maybe eight, frowned at him. __Then why do you always say it's almost done?__ Her mother hushed her, but the question stayed on the table like spilled tea. Somchai laughed too loudly and began packing the amplifier. Thuy watched him wind the cable around his arm, tighter and tighter, and understood that there was no new song, and perhaps had not been one for a long time.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals the girl's boredom with songs the duo has played too often.
It points out a flaw in Somchai's excuse that leads to Thuy's realization.
It shifts attention from the musicians to the girl's strict, watchful mother.
It suggests that the girl has already heard an early version of the song.
items.explanation: Somchai는 한 달 동안 모든 공연에서 새 노래가 아직 준비되지 않았다고 말해 왔다. 아이의 질문은 늘 거의 다 됐다고 하면서 왜 내놓지 않느냐는 모순을 드러내고, 이후 Somchai의 과한 웃음과 Thuy의 깨달음으로 이어진다. 따라서 변명의 허점을 짚어 Thuy의 깨달음을 이끈다는 B가 정답이다. A는 아이의 지루함으로 오해한 것이고, C와 D는 지문의 초점과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: We had been in Malek's radio repair shop in Woodstock for an hour, Amara and I, and the coach still had not mentioned the anniversary. It was ten years since the club's only championship; the board wanted a ceremony in Cape Town, and Amara, benched all season, had been asked to lead the parade. She wanted to refuse. Malek, who had coached her since she was eleven, kept his hands busy on a cracked radio from the stadium's old press box. __He had repaired that same radio before every final he had ever coached.__ When it finally crackled to life, he turned the dial to the station that had called the championship and set it on the counter between them. Amara listened to the old match replaying in a broadcaster's anniversary special and, after a long while, asked him what she should wear.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Amara has been kept on the bench for the whole season.
It suggests that Malek would rather fix radios than coach the team.
It hints that Malek's repair is his indirect answer about the anniversary.
It shows that the press box radio was damaged during the championship.
items.explanation: Malek은 기념일 이야기를 꺼내지 않고 라디오만 고치는데, 밑줄 문장은 그가 결승전마다 이 라디오를 고쳐 왔다는 의식 같은 의미를 알려 준다. 이후 그는 우승을 중계한 방송을 틀어 두고, Amara는 결국 무엇을 입을지 묻는다. 두 부분을 연결하면 밑줄 문장은 수리가 기념일에 대한 Malek의 간접적인 대답임을 암시하므로 C가 정답이다. B는 그럴듯하지만 코치 일을 꺼린다는 근거가 없고, A와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Saga had been folding dumplings wrong for three weeks before she told me about the offer. A hotel kitchen in Seoul wanted her, with a salary I could not match and a uniform with her name stitched on the pocket. I said nothing for a while and kept skimming the broth, which needs skimming whether or not anyone is leaving. When I was her age, I left a stall like this one and came back after a year, ashamed of how little the city had taught me. I did not tell her that. Some lessons spoil when they are handed over. Instead I showed her once more how to pinch the edge so the seam holds in boiling water, and I watched her hands rather than her face. Outside, the wind off the harbor rattled the plastic awning, and a customer called for a second bowl.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Saga's offer?
options: Open resentment toward Saga for considering a job that would leave the stall short of help
Quiet relief that Saga will soon leave a stall where she has struggled to learn the work
Private unease held in check by a belief that Saga must reach her own decision
Firm certainty that Saga will return once she finds the city has little to teach her
items.explanation: 화자는 제안을 듣고 한동안 말없이 국물만 걷어 내며 감정을 드러내지 않는다. 자신도 젊을 때 떠났다가 부끄럽게 돌아왔다는 경험을 말하지 않고 '어떤 교훈은 건네면 상한다'고 여기는 데서, 걱정은 있지만 Saga가 스스로 결정해야 한다고 믿는 태도가 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 노골적 원망이나 B의 안도는 근거가 없고, D는 화자의 과거 경험을 Saga의 미래에 대한 확신으로 잘못 확대한 것이다.

items.passage: When Amelie arrived at the laundromat on Calle Feria each afternoon, her grandfather Ivan was already scolding the dryers in a language she was only half learning. He had kept the place open for thirty-one years, through two floods and a decade in which the neighbors bought machines of their own. His ledger was a schoolchild's notebook, and its columns had been thinning for years; still he wrote the day's few coins in a careful hand, as if neatness might persuade the numbers. Amelie practiced verbs by reading his labels aloud: wash, wait, return. He corrected her accent with more patience than he ever showed the machines. Neither of them mentioned the letter from the landlord, folded under the coin tray where it had rested for a month. Down the street, a bakery lowered its shutter, and the smell of anise drifted in with the heat.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Ivan's efforts to keep the laundromat open?
options: Mocking, treating his careful bookkeeping as proof that he misunderstands basic arithmetic
Admiring, presenting his persistence as certain to restore the business to its old success
Indifferent, recording his habits without hinting that the business faces real difficulty
Tender yet realistic, honoring his diligence while noting signs that the business is failing
items.explanation: 서술자는 Ivan이 31년간 가게를 지켜 온 끈기와 정성스러운 장부 기록을 따뜻하게 그린다. 동시에 장부의 줄이 해마다 줄어들고 집주인의 편지가 한 달째 동전 접시 밑에 놓여 있다는 점을 짚어 가게가 기울고 있음을 분명히 한다. 이 두 단서를 함께 보면 D가 정답이다. A의 조롱, B의 낙관적 확신, C의 무관심은 이런 이중적 시선과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Film canisters rattled on the shelf when the power died, and I found myself stuck in a projection booth in Lima with a stranger named Sipho, who had come to repair the lens. For two hours we waited for the street to come back on. He told me that in his family a goodbye was never said at the door; you walked the guest to the corner, so the parting happened in open air. I had always considered such rituals a little theatrical. Yet when the lights returned and he packed his tools, I caught myself following him down the narrow stairs, past the ticket window, all the way to the end of the block. I am still not sure whose custom I was honoring. A bus went by with its windows fogged, carrying no one I knew.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Sipho's custom of parting?
options: Former skepticism that has softened into a reluctant, almost unconscious acceptance
Steady contempt for a custom that the narrator regards as needlessly theatrical
Nostalgic longing for a family tradition the narrator practiced as a young child
Polite curiosity that never affects how the narrator actually behaves toward Sipho
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 그런 의식을 '다소 연극적'이라고 여겼다고 밝힌다. 그러나 불이 들어오자 자신도 모르게 Sipho를 따라 골목 끝까지 걸어가며, 누구의 관습을 따른 것인지 모르겠다고 말한다. 두 부분을 연결하면 회의가 무의식적인 수용으로 바뀐 A가 정답이다. B는 앞부분만 본 오답이고, C는 지문에 없는 어린 시절을, D는 실제 행동 변화를 무시한다.

items.passage: Aunt Themba never wasted water. Each morning in the community garden off Mirpur Road, she filled one dented can and divided it among the chilies, the gourds, and Edith's struggling mint, giving the mint the least. Edith, who cooked for the stall her aunt ran, assumed this was a judgment on her. That afternoon a neighbor mentioned, as if everyone knew, that Themba had once given up a place at a teachers' college so that Edith's mother could finish school instead. Edith said nothing. Later, watering alone, she noticed that her aunt's own plot, the farthest from the tap, had always received the last and smallest share. A rickshaw bell sounded beyond the fence, and pigeons lifted off the tin roof of the tool shed.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how Edith learns that a neighbor knows private details of her family's past
To show Edith beginning to see her aunt's strictness as a pattern of quiet self-denial
To describe the daily routine of tending a crowded community garden in Dhaka
To suggest that every family hides sacrifices its younger members will never learn of
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Edith는 고모가 자기 민트에 물을 가장 적게 주는 것을 자신에 대한 평가로 받아들인다. 이웃에게서 고모가 동생을 위해 교대 입학을 포기했다는 사실을 들은 뒤, 고모 자신의 밭이 늘 가장 적은 물을 받아 왔다는 점을 알아차린다. 두 근거를 이으면 엄격함을 조용한 자기희생으로 다시 보게 되는 과정이 요지이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 소재만 같으며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Who pays a tutor in oranges? Miriam had asked this aloud the first week, when Fiorella refused her envelope of coins and accepted only a sack of fruit from the barge's hold. Since then the tutor had come every Thursday, climbing down the ladder with her books wrapped against the river damp, and Miriam's brother had begun reading the cargo lists to the crew with sudden pride. Miriam kept the coins in a tin, telling herself she would insist next time. But this evening she found her brother's old shoes, the pair that had split at the toe, replaced by a sturdy one, with a note in Fiorella's handwriting tucked inside: outgrown by my nephew. Miriam set the tin back on its shelf, unopened. Along the bank, a crane swung a pallet of cement toward a waiting truck.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how Miriam's brother improves his reading by studying cargo lists with the crew
To explain why Fiorella prefers to be paid in fruit rather than in coins for her lessons
To trace Miriam's shift from wanting to settle a debt to accepting Fiorella's kindness
To suggest that generosity between strangers always means more than any form of payment
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Miriam은 동전을 깡통에 모아 두며 다음에는 꼭 값을 치르겠다고 다짐한다. 그러나 Fiorella가 몰래 동생의 새 신발을 놓고 간 것을 발견한 뒤에는 깡통을 열지 않은 채 선반에 되돌려 놓는다. 이 대비에서 빚을 갚으려던 태도가 호의를 받아들이는 태도로 바뀌는 과정이 요지이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 세부 일화만, B는 소재는 같지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나친 일반화다.

items.passage: Moira and I spent most of one winter competing to sell pastries in the lobby of a cinema in Samarkand that showed films only on weekends. Each Friday I arrived early to claim the table beside the poster of a forgotten comedy, and each Friday she was already there, her trays set out in tight rows. I used to count her customers instead of serving my own. In February the projector broke, and for three weeks no one came at all. We sat on opposite benches, then on the same bench, trading samples out of boredom. I learned that she folded her dough twice where I folded mine four times, and that her version was better. When the films returned, I set up wherever there was space. Snow slid from the marquee in long, soft sheets.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe the narrator's rivalry with Moira over the best table in the cinema lobby
To explain the differences between two techniques for folding pastry dough
To argue that competition between small businesses usually harms everyone involved
To show how an enforced pause loosened the narrator's habit of rivalry with Moira
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 매주 좋은 자리를 차지하려 하고 자기 손님 대신 Moira의 손님 수를 셀 만큼 경쟁에 매여 있었다. 영사기가 고장 나 손님이 끊긴 동안 같은 벤치에 앉아 반죽법을 배우고, 영화가 다시 시작되자 아무 자리에나 가판을 차린다. 두 장면의 대비가 습관을 내려놓는 과정을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 앞부분 일화만, B는 소재만 같고, C는 지나치게 일반적인 주장이다.

items.passage: When the monsoon filled our cellar in Karachi, my twin, Nadeesha, and I had been dividing our late father's house for two months without once mentioning why he had left it to us in equal halves. We split the furniture by alternating choices, the books by shelf, the kitchen by drawer. Every list was polite and complete, and none of it touched the subject. The flood made lists useless. We waded in together, passing up boxes neither of us had labeled, and in one of them were letters he had written to each of us and never sent. We read them sitting on the stairs, our feet still in the water, and for the first time that year we argued, loudly, about him. By evening the pump had begun its slow work, coughing brown water into the lane.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To show how an accident broke the careful silence that had shaped the twins' dealings
To recount the method the twins used to divide their father's furniture and books
To describe the damage that a monsoon flood caused to a family home in Karachi
To suggest that arguments between siblings are a healthy part of every family's grief
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 쌍둥이는 가구와 책을 정중하게 나누면서도 아버지에 관한 핵심 주제는 한 번도 꺼내지 않는다. 홍수로 목록이 쓸모없어지고 부치지 않은 편지를 발견한 뒤, 그해 처음으로 아버지에 대해 크게 다툰다. 두 장면의 대비가 사고로 침묵이 깨지는 과정을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 소재는 같지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Rumors travel faster than buses. Xinyi, who had spent thirty years as a judge before retiring to the hills outside Hanoi, knew this better than most. Waiting at the mountain stop, she watched Nguyen, the young clerk from the district office, climb the road with his jaw set. Someone had carried to the landlord's wife what Nguyen had said about the landlord, and now the whole village was repeating it. Xinyi offered him half her bench. She had learned long ago that a story repeated often enough grows teeth, and that once it bites, no ruling can unsay it. She told him to apologize before evening, plainly and without excuses. Below them, mist filled the valley, and the bus horn sounded around the last bend.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “grows teeth” most nearly suggests that a repeated story
options: becomes more amusing to the villagers each time it is told
loses its details until it no longer resembles the original remark
gains the power to cause real harm to the people it concerns
grows so long that listeners eventually stop paying attention
items.explanation: 이야기가 이빨을 갖게 되면 '한번 물면 어떤 판결로도 되돌릴 수 없다'는 뒤 구절이 이 비유의 의미를 분명히 한다. 또한 Xinyi가 저녁이 되기 전에 사과하라고 서두르게 하는 데서 소문이 실제 해를 끼칠 수 있다는 위기감이 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 재미, B의 왜곡, D의 지루함은 '문다'는 이미지와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
By noon the riverbed is a road of cracked plates,
and Clement crosses it the way he pays his debts:
slowly, one stone at a time, never looking back.
Bogdan follows with the letter in his pocket,
the apology he wrote in March and never sent,
its corners softened now to cloth.
He owes his uncle money, and something more,
a sentence he carries like a stone in a shoe,
small enough to hide, too sharp to forget.
On the far bank a goat chews a plastic bag,
and the heat makes the hills tremble.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “like a stone in a shoe” most nearly suggests that the unsent apology
options: causes Bogdan a constant, private discomfort that he cannot ignore
weighs him down so heavily that he cannot cross the dry riverbed
protects Bogdan from the sharp stones scattered across the crossing
reminds him only of the sum of money he still owes his uncle
items.explanation: 부치지 못한 사과 편지는 모서리가 천처럼 닳을 만큼 오래 주머니에 들어 있었다. 비유 바로 뒤의 '숨길 만큼 작지만 잊기엔 너무 날카롭다'는 구절은 남에게 보이지 않지만 계속 신경 쓰이는 불편함을 뜻한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 무게로, C는 보호로 잘못 읽었고, D는 '그 이상의 무언가'라는 표현을 무시하고 돈만 떠올린 것이다.

items.passage: Secateurs clicked down every row of the vineyard that March in Auckland, but between Leilani and me there was only silence. She had taught me piano for six years, and when she invited me to play at her farewell concert, I said no, too quickly, and then could not explain why. For the whole harvest we worked the same slope without a word. Our silence was a vine grown across the path: each day it thickened, and each day it was harder to step over. I told myself she would speak first. She did not, and on the last afternoon I found her bucket left beside mine, half full of the grapes I had missed. I carried both to the truck. Wasps hung drowsy over the crushed fruit on the tarps.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a vine grown across the path” most nearly suggests that the silence between Leilani and the narrator
options: was a natural part of the quiet, focused work of harvesting grapes
protected the narrator from having to explain her refusal to anyone
became a more stubborn obstacle the longer it was left alone
signaled that their friendship would only continue to grow stronger
items.explanation: 비유 바로 뒤에 '날마다 굵어지고 날마다 넘어가기 더 어려워졌다'는 설명이 붙어, 침묵이 시간이 갈수록 넘기 힘든 장애물이 되었음을 보여 준다. 화자가 상대가 먼저 말하리라 기다리기만 했다는 점도 방치된 침묵이 더 굳어졌음을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 수확 작업의 고요함으로, B는 보호막으로, D는 '자란다'는 말을 우정의 성장으로 잘못 읽은 것이다.

## 문항
### lit40-medium-08-046 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Once, at the hour the ward lights dim to amber,
Mingyu asked me for a map of the old creek
that cut through his part of Shanghai before the city paved it.
I am Yuxuan, a nurse; I keep charts, not maps,
but I drew what he described on the back of one:
a footbridge, a willow, the dry stones he crossed in August
when the water had gone somewhere else to sleep.
He traced it with a finger that no longer trusted itself.
That is the way, he said, and closed his eyes.
I folded the chart into his pocket.
Every night since, I have walked a riverbed of linoleum,
listening for the water to come home.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a riverbed of linoleum” most nearly suggests that the speaker
A) resents the hospital for replacing the creek that once ran there.
B) has begun to sleepwalk through the ward during her night shifts.
C) still carries the patient's remembered route through her rounds.
D) believes the patient's map was too inaccurate to be followed.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
화자는 환자 Mingyu가 묘사한 마른 개울길을 차트 뒷면에 그려 주었고, 환자는 그것이 길이라고 말한 뒤 눈을 감는다. 이후 화자는 매일 밤 병동 바닥을 마른 강바닥처럼 걸으며 물이 돌아오기를 기다린다. 두 부분을 연결하면 이 비유는 화자가 환자의 기억 속 길을 일상의 순회 속에 계속 품고 다닌다는 뜻이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 원망의 근거가 없고, B는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽었으며, D는 지문 내용과 반대된다.
### lit40-medium-08-048 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Two rules governed the salt flat behind the house I rented outside Port of Spain: never walk on a pan that is still drying, and never rake against the wind. Shanice, my landlord, taught me both in my first month there, though I had only asked her about the leaking roof. She was the last person on that stretch of coast who still harvested salt by hand, and her own children had moved to offices in the city. She called me Alisha-girl, as if I were a niece rather than a tenant. Each evening she handed me the long wooden rake and corrected my wrist without comment. I assumed she simply wanted cheap help. Then, the summer she grew too ill to stand in the heat, she gave me the rake for good and called it the only lease she had ever meant. I rented that house eleven more years and never asked about the roof again.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “the only lease she had ever meant” most nearly suggests that Shanice viewed
A) teaching her craft as the true bond between her and the narrator.
B) the rental contract as a legal burden she wished to end quickly.
C) the rake as payment owed to her for many years of unpaid rent.
D) her illness as a reason to sell the salt flat to the narrator.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
Shanice는 자녀들이 도시로 떠난 뒤 해안에서 손으로 소금을 거두는 마지막 사람이며, 세입자인 화자를 조카처럼 부르며 매일 기술을 가르친다. 병들어 일을 못 하게 되자 갈퀴를 넘겨주며 이것이 자신이 진심으로 맺은 유일한 계약이라고 말한다. 두 단서를 종합하면 기술을 물려주는 일이 두 사람 사이의 진짜 약속이었다는 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 임대 계약이나 금전 관계를 문자 그대로 해석한 오답이다.
### lit40-medium-08-054 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
On Tuesdays at four, Matheus brought the pharmacy order to the hospital waiting room in Porto Alegre, and on Tuesdays at four Putri was already there, folding the free newspapers into neat stacks for the volunteers. She had started the chore while her husband was a patient upstairs; she kept at it, she told Matheus briskly, only because the stacks were always a mess and someone had to fix them. He usually helped with the last pile before running to his next delivery. This week he arrived to find the papers already folded and Putri sitting with her hands empty in her lap. The volunteers had hired a cleaner, she said. Then, after a pause, she asked whether he might sit a moment anyway, since she no longer knew what to do with four o'clock.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) It moves from brisk practicality to a quiet admission of loneliness.
B) It moves from cheerful nostalgia to open anger at the volunteers.
C) It moves from anxious worry about a patient to calm, settled relief.
D) It moves from playful teasing to stiff, formal politeness toward Matheus.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
앞부분에서 Putri는 신문 접기를 누군가 해야 할 일일 뿐이라고 사무적으로 말한다. 그러나 일이 사라지자 빈손으로 앉아 있다가 네 시를 어떻게 보내야 할지 모르겠다며 잠시 앉아 달라고 부탁한다. 두 장면을 연결하면 실용적인 어조가 조용한 외로움의 고백으로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B의 분노, C의 환자 걱정, D의 농담은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-08-055 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
When Soren came home to the beekeeper's yard in Manila, he went straight to the hive their father had built, the one whose roof had split in the typhoon two years before. Kaya watched from the porch as he measured, sawed, and nailed with the energy of a man following orders, whistling and announcing every step: new cedar, tighter joints, good as before. She brought him water and laughed when a bee settled in his hair. By late afternoon the roof was whole. Soren stood back to admire it, and the whistling stopped. The bees had moved long ago to a hollow in the mango tree, and none of them came near the box. He set the hammer down very carefully, as though it might break, and asked Kaya, without turning, how long they had been gone.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) It moves from tense suspicion between siblings to relieved good cheer.
B) It moves from bustling confidence to a subdued, sorrowful recognition.
C) It moves from mournful reflection on the past to firm optimism.
D) It moves from playful rivalry to open resentment of his sister.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
앞부분의 Soren은 휘파람을 불며 작업 단계를 하나하나 외치는 자신감 넘치는 모습이다. 그러나 지붕을 다 고친 뒤 벌들이 오래전에 떠났다는 사실을 깨닫자 휘파람이 멈추고 망치를 조심스럽게 내려놓으며 조용히 묻는다. 두 장면의 대비는 분주한 자신감에서 가라앉은 슬픈 깨달음으로의 전환을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 전환 방향이 반대이고, D의 원망은 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-08-056 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
Dayoung had not spoken to me for two years when she mailed me a swimsuit, plain navy and one size too large. I read it as an insult, a remark on the weight I had gained after my divorce, and I left it in its box. Last month, in Busan for our aunt's birthday, I went alone to the salt-water pool by the breakwater where we had swum as girls. Dongsik, the attendant who had worked there since we were children, recognized me at once. He said my sister came every Sunday and always asked whether I had been in. Then he pointed to the lockers. Hers still bore a tag with both our names, written in the round letters of a ten-year-old. I stood a long time in the wet air, thinking of the navy suit, bought large the way our mother always bought clothes for girls she expected to grow.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) It moves from nostalgic warmth to bitter disappointment in a sister.
B) It moves from detached humor to anxious urgency about a reunion.
C) It moves from wounded suspicion to softened, regretful understanding.
D) It moves from calm curiosity to outright joy at meeting a sister.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
처음에 화자는 큰 수영복을 체중에 대한 모욕으로 받아들이고 상자에 넣어 둔다. 그러나 수영장에서 언니가 매주 자신을 찾았다는 말과 두 사람의 이름이 적힌 사물함을 본 뒤, 수영복을 어머니가 자랄 아이에게 옷을 사 주던 방식과 연결한다. 이 흐름은 상처받은 의심에서 누그러진 후회 섞인 이해로의 전환이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 방향이 반대이고, B와 D는 지문에 없는 감정이다.
### lit40-medium-08-057 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Although the night-shift pharmacy on Calle Zanja sold only aspirin and cough syrup after midnight, Wenhua sat there every night that week, because its phone was the only one on the block that still worked. His daughter sat beside him with a dictionary, since the call would come from the embassy in English. Booker, the pharmacist, pretended not to notice them and kept the radio low. For hours nothing happened: the fan turned, a taxi driver bought antacid, Wenhua smoothed the same receipt over and over. At four in the morning the phone rang. His daughter listened, said yes three times, and hung up. Before she could translate, Wenhua read her face and began to laugh, and Booker, who had understood nothing, turned the radio all the way up.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It introduces a conflict between a father and daughter and then shows a stranger resolving it.
B) It describes a pharmacy's nightly routine and then explains why that routine is about to end.
C) It recounts a phone call in detail and then reflects on its lasting effects on a family.
D) It depicts a long, uneventful wait and then shifts to the moment the news arrives.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
지문 앞부분은 아버지와 딸이 대사관의 전화를 기다리며 아무 일도 일어나지 않는 긴 밤을 묘사한다. 새벽 네 시에 전화가 울리면서 초점은 소식이 도착하는 순간과 그에 대한 반응으로 옮겨 간다. 따라서 긴 기다림에서 소식 도착으로 이동하는 D가 구조를 정확히 설명한다. A의 부녀 갈등과 B의 일과 종료는 근거가 없고, C는 통화 내용이나 장기적 결과를 다루지 않는다는 점에서 틀리다.
### lit40-medium-08-059 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
"Play the new one," the girl at the corner table called, the moment Thuy and Somchai finished their set at the roadside diner outside Surabaya. Somchai smiled and said the new song wasn't ready yet. He had said the same thing at every stop for a month. Thuy tuned her guitar and said nothing; she had stopped asking him where the new songs were. The girl, maybe eight, frowned at him. __Then why do you always say it's almost done?__ Her mother hushed her, but the question stayed on the table like spilled tea. Somchai laughed too loudly and began packing the amplifier. Thuy watched him wind the cable around his arm, tighter and tighter, and understood that there was no new song, and perhaps had not been one for a long time.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It reveals the girl's boredom with songs the duo has played too often.
B) It points out a flaw in Somchai's excuse that leads to Thuy's realization.
C) It shifts attention from the musicians to the girl's strict, watchful mother.
D) It suggests that the girl has already heard an early version of the song.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
Somchai는 한 달 동안 모든 공연에서 새 노래가 아직 준비되지 않았다고 말해 왔다. 아이의 질문은 늘 거의 다 됐다고 하면서 왜 내놓지 않느냐는 모순을 드러내고, 이후 Somchai의 과한 웃음과 Thuy의 깨달음으로 이어진다. 따라서 변명의 허점을 짚어 Thuy의 깨달음을 이끈다는 B가 정답이다. A는 아이의 지루함으로 오해한 것이고, C와 D는 지문의 초점과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-08-060 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
We had been in Malek's radio repair shop in Woodstock for an hour, Amara and I, and the coach still had not mentioned the anniversary. It was ten years since the club's only championship; the board wanted a ceremony in Cape Town, and Amara, benched all season, had been asked to lead the parade. She wanted to refuse. Malek, who had coached her since she was eleven, kept his hands busy on a cracked radio from the stadium's old press box. __He had repaired that same radio before every final he had ever coached.__ When it finally crackled to life, he turned the dial to the station that had called the championship and set it on the counter between them. Amara listened to the old match replaying in a broadcaster's anniversary special and, after a long while, asked him what she should wear.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It explains why Amara has been kept on the bench for the whole season.
B) It suggests that Malek would rather fix radios than coach the team.
C) It hints that Malek's repair is his indirect answer about the anniversary.
D) It shows that the press box radio was damaged during the championship.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Malek은 기념일 이야기를 꺼내지 않고 라디오만 고치는데, 밑줄 문장은 그가 결승전마다 이 라디오를 고쳐 왔다는 의식 같은 의미를 알려 준다. 이후 그는 우승을 중계한 방송을 틀어 두고, Amara는 결국 무엇을 입을지 묻는다. 두 부분을 연결하면 밑줄 문장은 수리가 기념일에 대한 Malek의 간접적인 대답임을 암시하므로 C가 정답이다. B는 그럴듯하지만 코치 일을 꺼린다는 근거가 없고, A와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-08-061 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

A hotel kitchen in Seoul wanted her, with a salary I could not match and a uniform with her name stitched on the pocket. I said nothing for a while and kept skimming the broth, which needs skimming whether or not anyone is leaving. When I was her age, I left a stall like this one and came back after a year, ashamed of how little the city had taught me. I did not tell her that. Some lessons spoil when they are handed over. Instead I showed her once more how to pinch the edge so the seam holds in boiling water, and I watched her hands rather than her face. Outside, the wind off the harbor rattled the plastic awning, and a customer called for a second bowl.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Saga's offer?
A) Open resentment toward Saga for considering a job that would leave the stall short of help
B) Quiet relief that Saga will soon leave a stall where she has struggled to learn the work
C) Private unease held in check by a belief that Saga must reach her own decision
D) Firm certainty that Saga will return once she finds the city has little to teach her

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
화자는 제안을 듣고 한동안 말없이 국물만 걷어 내며 감정을 드러내지 않는다. 자신도 젊을 때 떠났다가 부끄럽게 돌아왔다는 경험을 말하지 않고 '어떤 교훈은 건네면 상한다'고 여기는 데서, 걱정은 있지만 Saga가 스스로 결정해야 한다고 믿는 태도가 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 노골적 원망이나 B의 안도는 근거가 없고, D는 화자의 과거 경험을 Saga의 미래에 대한 확신으로 잘못 확대한 것이다.
### lit40-medium-08-062 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

His ledger was a schoolchild's notebook, and its columns had been thinning for years; still he wrote the day's few coins in a careful hand, as if neatness might persuade the numbers. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Ivan's efforts to keep the laundromat open?
A) Mocking, treating his careful bookkeeping as proof that he misunderstands basic arithmetic
B) Admiring, presenting his persistence as certain to restore the business to its old success
C) Indifferent, recording his habits without hinting that the business faces real difficulty
D) Tender yet realistic, honoring his diligence while noting signs that the business is failing

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
서술자는 Ivan이 31년간 가게를 지켜 온 끈기와 정성스러운 장부 기록을 따뜻하게 그린다. 동시에 장부의 줄이 해마다 줄어들고 집주인의 편지가 한 달째 동전 접시 밑에 놓여 있다는 점을 짚어 가게가 기울고 있음을 분명히 한다. 이 두 단서를 함께 보면 D가 정답이다. A의 조롱, B의 낙관적 확신, C의 무관심은 이런 이중적 시선과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-08-063 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

I had always considered such rituals a little theatrical. Yet when the lights returned and he packed his tools, I caught myself following him down the narrow stairs, past the ticket window, all the way to the end of the block. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Sipho's custom of parting?
A) Former skepticism that has softened into a reluctant, almost unconscious acceptance
B) Steady contempt for a custom that the narrator regards as needlessly theatrical
C) Nostalgic longing for a family tradition the narrator practiced as a young child
D) Polite curiosity that never affects how the narrator actually behaves toward Sipho

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
화자는 처음에 그런 의식을 '다소 연극적'이라고 여겼다고 밝힌다. 그러나 불이 들어오자 자신도 모르게 Sipho를 따라 골목 끝까지 걸어가며, 누구의 관습을 따른 것인지 모르겠다고 말한다. 두 부분을 연결하면 회의가 무의식적인 수용으로 바뀐 A가 정답이다. B는 앞부분만 본 오답이고, C는 지문에 없는 어린 시절을, D는 실제 행동 변화를 무시한다.
### lit40-medium-08-064 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]

That afternoon a neighbor mentioned, as if everyone knew, that Themba had once given up a place at a teachers' college so that Edith's mother could finish school instead. Edith said nothing. [질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) To recount how Edith learns that a neighbor knows private details of her family's past
B) To show Edith beginning to see her aunt's strictness as a pattern of quiet self-denial
C) To describe the daily routine of tending a crowded community garden in Dhaka

앞부분에서 Edith는 고모가 자기 민트에 물을 가장 적게 주는 것을 자신에 대한 평가로 받아들인다. 이웃에게서 고모가 동생을 위해 교대 입학을 포기했다는 사실을 들은 뒤, 고모 자신의 밭이 늘 가장 적은 물을 받아 왔다는 점을 알아차린다. 두 근거를 이으면 엄격함을 조용한 자기희생으로 다시 보게 되는 과정이 요지이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 소재만 같으며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-08-065 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose

### lit40-medium-08-066 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose

### lit40-medium-08-069 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]

Someone had carried to the landlord's wife what Nguyen had said about the landlord, and now the whole village was repeating it. Xinyi offered him half her bench. ### lit40-medium-08-071 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language

### lit40-medium-08-073 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “a vine grown across the path” most nearly suggests that the silence between Leilani and the narrator
